akhfash:1-2.t: ﴿لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾, that is: He did that for the bringing together (īlāf) of Quraysh, for (their) uniting (لتألّف); then He substituted (with a badal) and said ﴿إِيلاَفِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ ٱلشِّتَآءِ وَٱلصَّيْفِ﴾, because it is from "أَلَفَ"*. And some read ﴿لإِيلاَفِ﴾, taking it from "آلَفُوا". «[Translator's note: the two readings are printed identically in the source, so the difference between them is not visible in the text as transmitted.]»

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿إِيلَافِهِمْ﴾: a tawkīd (emphasis); it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «آلف» with the long vowel (madd). ﴿رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ﴾ to Yemen ﴿وَ﴾ the journey of ﴿الصَّيْفِ﴾ to al-Shām every year; they used the two journeys for trade to help them in staying in Mecca to serve the House, which is their pride. They are the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kināna.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُوا﴾: «لإيلاف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) it, and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida). ﴿رَبَّ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ﴾

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ﴾, that is, because of it, ﴿وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ﴾, that is, because of it. Hunger used to afflict them because there was no cultivation in Mecca, and they feared the army of the elephant.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿لِإِيلافِ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the later verb ليعبدوا. ﴿قُرَيْشٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿إِيلافِهِمْ﴾ a badal (substitute) from what precedes it. ﴿رِحْلَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun). ﴿الشِّتاءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالصَّيْفِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الشتاء.

daas-irab:3-3.t: [Translator's note: the word markers in the source text of this entry are garbled; the Quranic words are restored here as ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُوا﴾, ﴿رَبَّ هذَا﴾ and ﴿الْبَيْتِ﴾.] ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ implying an unstated condition), and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the lām, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبَّ هذَا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to the demonstrative. ﴿الْبَيْتِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, a badal (substitute) from رب. ﴿أَطْعَمَهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ جُوعٍ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

farraa:1-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾.
Someone may ask: how can speech begin with a lām that puts [a noun] in the genitive, with nothing after it that is made nominative by it? The answer to that is in two ways.
Some of them said: [149/b] it was joined to ﴿ألم تر كيف فعل ربك﴾. That is because He reminded the people of Mecca of the greatness of His blessing upon them in what He did to the Abyssinians; then He said: ﴿لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيشٍ﴾ as well, as though He said: that [is added] to His blessing upon them in the journey of winter and summer. You say: نعمة إلى نعمة (a blessing added to a blessing) and نعمة لنعمة, the same in meaning.
And it is said that He, Blessed and Exalted is He, made His Prophet ﷺ wonder, saying: Wonder, O Muhammad, at the blessings of Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, upon Quraysh in their being accustomed to (إيلافهم) the journey of winter and summer. Then He said: so let them not be distracted by that from following you and from believing in Allah: ﴿فَلْيَعْبُدُواْ رَبَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْبَيْتِ﴾. As for "الإيلاف", ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with yāʾ after the hamza; some of the people of Medina read it "إلا فِهم", shortened, in both words; and some readers read: (إلْفِهم). All are correct. They did not differ on the accusative of «الرحلة», by «الإيلاف» acting upon it. Were someone to put it in the genitive, he would make «الرحلة» be the «الإيلاف» itself, as in your saying: العجبُ لرحلتهم شتاء وصيفا (Wonder at their journey in winter and summer). And had one put إيلافَهم or إلفَهم in the accusative, making it a maṣdar (verbal noun) and not repeating it upon the beginning of the speech, it would be correct; as though you said: العجب لدخولك دخولا دارَنا (wonder at your entering — an entering — our house). «الإيلاف», though annexed, would be of this meaning, as He said: ﴿إذا زُلْزِلَتِ الأَرْضُ زِلْزَالَهَا﴾.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَطْعَمَهُم مِّن جُوعٍ﴾.
After the years [of drought] that afflicted them, so that they ate carrion and dead animals. Then Syria became fertile and [provisions] were carried to al-Abṭaḥ, and Yemen became fertile and [provisions] were carried to Jedda. He says: Allah brought them provision from two directions and spared them the two journeys; so if they follow you and keep to the House, Allah will spare them the two journeys too, as He [already] spared them.
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَآمَنَهُم مِّنْ خَوْفٍ﴾.
It is said: it is a secure land. And it is said: «من الخوف»: from leprosy; they were spared that, and there was no leprosy there at that time. The journey of winter was [150/a] to Syria and the journey of summer to Yemen. Whoever read "إلفهم", it may be from يُؤلَفون; and better than that is that it be from [يألفون (they are accustomed to) the journey of winter and the journey of summer; and «الإيلاف» is] from يؤلِفون, i.e. they make ready and equip [the caravans].

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition «لإيلاف» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يعبدوا» in verse (3).

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: «إيلافهم»: badal (substitute) of «إيلاف»; «رحلة»: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) «إيلافهم».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the lām is that of command, and the verb is jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the nūn; «هذا»: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (لإيلاف): the lām, according to al-Akhfash, is attached to (mutaʿalliq) His saying (فجعلهم كعصف), i.e. He did that to them so that Quraysh might be united; but there is remoteness in this, because of the consensus of all on the permissibility of pausing at the end of (ألم تر). And it was said: the lām is attached to an implied verb, its implied form being «اعجبوا لإيلاف قريش رحلة الشتاء والصيف وتركهم عبادة رب هذا البيت» (marvel at the uniting of Quraysh in the journey of winter and summer, and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House); this is the position of al-Farrāʾ. Al-Khalīl said: the lām is attached to His saying (فليعبدوا), as though He said: because Allah united Quraysh in a uniting, let them worship the Lord of this House.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (إيلافهم): a badal (substitute) for the first, for additional clarity, as you say «سمعت كلامك كلامك زيدا». (إيلاف) is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of a quadriliteral verb. Whoever read it «إلفهم» made it the maṣdar of a triliteral verb. Al-Farrāʾ allowed «إيلافَهم» in the accusative as a maṣdar.
His saying (رحلة الشتاء): accusative by (إيلافهم). There are two dialects in it, reported by Abū ʿUbayd: «ألِفته» and «آلفته»; and on that basis it was read (لإيلاف) and «لإلاف», from «ألف» and from «آلف». [Translator's note: the printed text has «وءلالف», evidently a corruption of the second reading.]

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿لإيلاف﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿فليعبدوا﴾.
﴿قريش﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿إيلافهم﴾: a badal (substitute) for the first «إيلاف», genitive (majrūr) by the kasra, and it is muḍāf; the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable (mabnī) on the kasra in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural.
﴿رحلة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the maṣdar (verbal noun) «إيلافهم», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿الشتاء﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra.
﴿والصيف﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «الصيف» is conjoined to «الشتاء», genitive by the kasra.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿فليعبدوا﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ of eloquence (al-faṣīḥa), because it occurs in the answer of an implied condition, i.e. "if they do not worship Him for the rest of His blessings, then let them worship Him for their familiarity, for it is the most evident of His blessings upon them" (إن لم يعبدوه لسائر نعمه فليعبدوه لإيلافهم فإنه أظهر نعمه عليهم); the lām is the lām of command, and «يعبدوا» is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, because it is one of the five verbs, and the wāw of the plural is a pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent).
﴿رب﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and it is muḍāf.
﴿هذا﴾: «ها» is for alerting, and «ذا» is a demonstrative indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿البيت﴾: a badal (substitute) for the demonstrative, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause ﴿يعبدوا﴾ is in the position of jussive as the answer of the implied condition.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «رب», or a badal (substitute) for it.
﴿أطعمهم﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "He" (هو); the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿أطعمهم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿من جوع﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أطعمهم﴾.
﴿وآمنهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «آمنهم» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and its agent is latent, its implied form being "He" (هو); the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the clause ﴿آمنهم﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿أطعمهم﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿من خوف﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿آمنهم﴾.

nahhas-irab:1-2.t:
لِإِيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ (1): the position of al-Akhfash is that the meaning is: He did that to them (the People of the Elephant) in order to bring Quraysh together in familiarity.
The error in this view is evident: if it were as he said, لإيلاف would be one of the verses of «ألم تر» (Sūrat al-Fīl), and in the consensus of the Muslims on separating them there is what indicates otherwise than what he said. Also, if it were as he said, the end of the (preceding) sūra would not be complete, and this is not found in any of the sūras. It has been said that there is an omission in the speech, the meaning being: "Marvel at the familiarity (īlāf) of Quraysh — رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ — and their abandoning the worship of the Lord of this House". This, I mean the omission, is the position of al-Farrāʾ, and it is argued for on the basis that the Arabs say لله أبوك ("to Allah [belongs] your father!"), so that the lām carries the sense of wonder. More correct than these two views — and it is the view of al-Khalīl ibn Aḥmad — is that the meaning is: "for Allah's bringing Quraysh together in familiarity".

nahhas-irab:3-3.t:
I.e., for this, let them worship Him. Abū Jaʿfar said: In this there is no omission, and it is among the fine and subtle points of grammar, even though the authors of the books of Maʿānī overlooked it. «إلفهم» (i.e., إِيلافِهِمْ) is genitive as a badal (substitute), as you say: عجبت من إحسانك إحسانك إلى زيد ("I marvelled at your kindness — your kindness to Zayd"): you substitute the second for the first and add to the information for clarification. It is narrated from Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ that he read «إلفهم», and «إلافهم» is also narrated from him; they are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) of alifa yaʾlafu, on the patterns fiʿl and fiʿāl. Fiʿl is like their saying ḥalama ḥilman, ʿalima ʿilman and sakhira sikhran; and fiʿāl is like laqītuhu liqāʾan, ṣumtu ṣiyāman and katabtu kitāban. Al-Farrāʾ permitted لِإِيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ إِيلافِهِمْ as a maṣdar [Translator's note: the context implies the accusative, إِيلافَهُمْ, though the printed vowelling shows the genitive]. Abū Jaʿfar said: The accusative is also permissible in إلفهم and إيلافهم, in the sense of "they become familiar with a familiarity". رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ is accusative by إيلاف; and al-Farrāʾ permitted إيلافهم رحلةِ الشتاء والصّيف (in the genitive). Abū Jaʿfar said: This would be by way of badal, its implied form being: "their familiarity, the familiarity with the journey of winter and summer".
فَلْيَعْبُدُوا رَبَّ هذَا الْبَيْتِ (3): and if you wish, you may give the lām kasra according to its origin.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t: الَّذِي is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of ربّ; it may also be in the position of the nominative, i.e., "He is the One who". أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذي, and وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ is included in the ṣila.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {مِّن جُوعٍ} and {مِّنْ خَوْفٍ}: for cause (li-l-taʿlīl), that is, "because of hunger and fear"; the indefiniteness is for magnification (li-l-taʿẓīm), that is, "from great hunger and great fear". Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It may be in the position of ḥāl from the object of «أَطْعَمهم»." Nāfiʿ, in one report, concealed the nūn of «مِنْ» before the khāʾ (ikhfāʾ), and likewise before the ghayn; this is a dialect that Sībawayh related.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {لإِيلاَفِ قُرَيْشٍ}: concerning what this lām is attached to, there are several views. The first: that it is what is in the preceding sūra, namely His saying {فَجَعَلَهُمْ كَعَصْفٍ} [al-Fīl: 5]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This is like enjambment (al-taḍmīn) in poetry", which is that the meaning of one verse depends on the one before it with a dependence that is sound only through it. In the codex of Ubayy the two are a single sūra without a break. It is reported from ʿUmar that he recited them in the second rakʿa of the sunset prayer, having recited {والتين} in the first. End of quotation. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash held this view, except that al-Ḥawfī said: "A group rejected this view, because if it were so, «لإِيلافِ» would be part of the sūra «ألم تَرَ», yet the unanimous agreement of all on the separation between the two shows that it is not so."
The second: that it is implied, the implied form being "we did that", that is, the destruction of the Companions of the Elephant, "for the familiarity (īlāf) of Quraysh". It was also said that the implied form is «اعْجَبوا» ("marvel!"). The third: that it is His saying «فَلْيَعْبُدوا». The fāʾ entered only because of the sense of condition in the sentence, that is: "if they do not worship Him for all His other favours, let them worship Him for their familiarity, for it is the most evident of His favours to them." Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is the view of al-Khalīl before him.
Ibn ʿĀmir read «لإِلافِ» without a yāʾ before the second lām, and the others read «لإِيلافِ» with a yāʾ before it. All agreed on keeping the yāʾ in the second, which is «إيلافِهِمْ». Among the curious things that occurred with these two words is that the readers differed on the dropping and keeping of the yāʾ in the first, although the codices agree on its being written, and they agreed on keeping the yāʾ in the second, although the codices agree on its being dropped in writing. This is the clearest proof that the readers follow the transmitted report and the narration and not merely the script.
As for the reading of Ibn ʿĀmir, there are two views on it. The first: that it is a maṣdar of the triliteral «alifa»; one says "alif-tuhu ilāfan", like "katabtuhu kitāban"; one says "alif-tuhu ilfan" and "ilāfan". The poet combined the two in his saying:
4647 - زَعَمْتُمْ أنَّ إخْوَتَكُمْ قُرَيْشٌ ... لهم إلْفٌ وليس لكُمْ إلافُ
(You claimed that your brothers are Quraysh; they have familiarity (ilf), and you have no familiarity (ilāf).)
The second: that it is the maṣdar of the quadriliteral «ālafa», like "qātala, qitālan". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "that is, for the association (muʾālafa) of Quraysh."
As for the reading of the others, it is the maṣdar of the quadriliteral «ālafa» on the pattern of «akrama»; one says "ālaftuhu, uʾlifuhu, īlāfan". The poet said:
4648 - مِنَ المُؤْلِفاتِ الرَّمْلِ أَدْماءُ حُرَّةٍ ... شعاعُ الضُّحى في مَتْنِها يَتَوضَّحُ
(From among the sand-dwelling does, a pure white noble she-camel; the rays of the forenoon show clear on her back.)
ʿĀṣim in one report read «إإْلافِهم» with two hamzas, the first with kasra and the second quiescent. This is irregular, because in such a case the second must be changed into a homogeneous letter, as in «īmān». It is also reported from him with two hamzas, both with kasra, followed by a quiescent yāʾ. This was explained as the second hamza's kasra having been lengthened so that a yāʾ was generated from it; this is more irregular than the first. Abū l-Baqāʾ transmitted something yet more irregular than it, saying: "with a hamza with kasra, followed by a quiescent yāʾ, followed by a hamza with kasra; this is remote. Its explanation is that he lengthened the kasra, from which the yāʾ arose, and he intended thereby to separate the two hamzas, like the alif in {أَأَنذَرْتَهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 6]."
Abū Jaʿfar read «لإِلْفِ قُرَيْشٍ» on the pattern of «qird». It was already mentioned that it is a maṣdar of «alifa», as in:
4649 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... لهم إلْفٌ وليس لكم إلافُ
(. . . they have familiarity (ilf), and you have no familiarity (ilāf).)
From him too, and from Ibn Kathīr, «إلْفِهم»; and from him too, and from Ibn ʿĀmir, «إلا فِهِمْ» like «kitābihim». And from him also «لِيْلافِ» with a quiescent yāʾ after the lām; this is because when he changed the second hamza he dropped the first, contrary to analogy. ʿIkrima read «لِتَأْلَفْ قُرَيْش» as an imperfect verb, and from him «لِيَأْلَفْ» as an imperative, with the lām with kasra; and from him a fatḥa on it with the imperative, which is a minor dialect.
Quraysh is the name of a tribe. It was said that they are the descendants of al-Naḍr ibn Kināna, and everyone whom al-Naḍr fathered is Qurashī, excluding Kināna; and this is the correct view. It was also said that they are the descendants of Fihr ibn Mālik ibn al-Naḍr ibn Kināna; whoever was not fathered by Fihr is not a Qurashī. Agreement was thus reached that the sons of Fihr are Qurashīs and that Kināna are not Qurashīs; the disagreement was over al-Naḍr and Mālik.
There was disagreement over its derivation, on several lines. The first: that it is from «taqarrush», which is gathering; they were so named because they came together after having been dispersed. The poet said:
4650 - أبونا قُصَيُّ كان يدعى مُجَمِّعاً ... به جَمَّعَ اللَّهُ القبائلَ مِنْ فِهْرِ
(Our father Quṣayy used to be called "the gatherer"; through him Allah gathered the tribes of Fihr.)
The second: that it is from «al-qarsh», which is earning. Quraysh were merchants. One says "qarasha, yaqrishu", that is, he earned. The third: that it is from inspection (al-tafṭīsh). One says "qarrasha yuqarrishu ʿannī", that is, he inspected. Quraysh used to inspect their friends in order to meet their needs. The poet said:
4651 - أيُّها الشامِتُ المُقَرِّشُ عنا ... عند عمروٍ فهَلْ له إبْقاءُ
(O you who gloat and spy on us at ʿAmr's, is there any mercy in him?)
Muʿāwiya asked Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "It was named after a creature of the sea called al-qirsh, which eats and is not eaten, overcomes and is not overcome." And he recited the saying of Tubbaʿ:
4652 - وَقُرَيْشٌ هي التي تَسْكُنُ البَحْ ... رَ سُمِّيَتْ قُرَيْشٌ قُرَيْشَا
تأكلُ الغَثَّ والسَّمينَ ولا تَتْ ... رُكُ فيها لذي جناحَيْنِ رِيشا
هكذا في البلادِ حَيُّ قُرَيْشٍ ... يأكلونَ البلادَ أكْلاً كَميشا
ولهم آخِرَ الزمان نَبيٌّ ... يُكْثِرُ القَتْلَ فيهمُ والخُموشا
(Quraysh is the one that dwells in the sea; Quraysh was named "Quraysh". It eats the lean and the fat, and leaves no feather for any winged creature. So too in the lands the clan of Quraysh devour the lands with a hasty devouring. And at the end of time they will have a prophet who will bring much killing and scratching among them.)
Then Quraysh is either a diminutive of a word with more than three radicals, in which case its diminutive is a diminutive of truncation (taṣghīr tarkhīm), and it was said that the original is «muqrish», or «qārish»; or it is a diminutive of a triliteral such as «al-qarsh». They agreed that it is inflected (maṣrūf) here, the clan being intended by it; had the tribe been intended, it would have been diptote (mamnūʿ min al-ṣarf), as in the saying of the poet:
465 - 3- غَلَبَ المَساميحَ الوليدُ سَماحةً ... وكفى قُرَيْشَ المُعْضِلاتِ وسادَها
(Al-Walīd surpassed the generous in generosity, and spared Quraysh its hard matters, and led them.)
[Translator's note: the verse number is printed as «465 - 3-», evidently 4653.]
Sībawayh said of Maʿadd, Quraysh, Thaqīf and Kināna: "These are for clans; and if you make it a name for tribes, that is permissible and good."
His saying: {إِيلاَفِهِمْ}: an emphasis of the first, a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī); for this reason it is attached to the pronoun of the one to whom the first was annexed, as you say: "I honoured Zayd for his standing, for his standing" (li-qiyāmi Zayd li-qiyāmihi akramtuhu). Abū l-Baqāʾ parsed it as a badal, but the first is better.
His saying: {رِحْلَةَ}: an object of the maṣdar, the maṣdar being annexed to its agent, that is, "because they became familiar with the journey". The original is "the two journeys of winter and summer", but it was put in the singular because there is no risk of confusion, as in his saying:
4654 - كُلوا في بَعْضِ بطنِكُمُ تَعِفُّوا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Eat in part of your bellies, and you will be chaste . . .)
Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is open to question, since Sībawayh treats this as poetic licence (ḍarūra), as in his saying:
4655 - حَمامةً بَطْنِ الوادِيَيْنِ تَرَنَّمي ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(O dove of the belly of the two valleys, coo . . .)
It was also said that «رِحْلة» is a generic noun (ism jins); they had four journeys. Some made it a mistake, but it is not so. The majority read it with kasra on the rāʾ, and it is a maṣdar; Abū l-Sammāl read it with ḍamma, and it is the destination to which one journeys.
Al-shitāʾ (winter) has a wāw as its lām (third radical), from their saying «al-shatwa» and «shatā yashtū». They deviated in forming the relative adjective from it, saying «shatawī»; the analogy is «shitāʾī» or «shitāwī», like «kisāʾī» and «kisāwī».

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
[Translator's note: the entry opens with a detached line, apparently a marginal gloss on «قُرَيْش»:] It is a diminutive of truncation (taṣghīr al-tarkhīm), because «الْقَرْش» is gathering, and the agent noun is «قَارِش», so by analogy [its diminutive] would be «قُوَيْرِش»; it was truncated and made diminutive.
Allah the Exalted said: (لِإِيلَافِ قُرَيْشٍ (١) إِيلَافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتَاءِ وَالصَّيْفِ (٢)).
The «lām» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the words of the Exalted (فَلْيَعْبُدُوا), i.e. let them worship Allah the Exalted because of their familiarity, and the [fāʾ] does not prevent that.
It is also said that it is attached to «جَعَلَهُمْ» in the preceding sūra, because the two are like a single sūra.
It is also said that the implied form is: «اعْجَبُوا لِإِيلَافٍ» (marvel at the familiarity). There are [several] readings of it. The first: «إِلْف», which is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «أَلِفَ يَأْلَفُ». The second: «إِلَاف», like «كِتَاب» and «قِيَام». The third: «إِيلَاف», whose verb is «آلَفَ» with a long vowel.
The fourth: «إِئْلَاف», with two hamzas, produced according to the original form; it is anomalous (shādhdh) in usage [and in analogy]. The fifth: with a hamza bearing kasra, followed by a vowelless yāʾ, followed by a hamza bearing kasra; this is far-fetched, and its justification is that the reader lengthened the kasra so that the yāʾ arose, intending thereby to separate the two hamzas, like the alif in «أَأَنْذَرْتَهُمْ».
(إِيلَافِ) is a badal (substitute) for the first. (رِحْلَةَ) is governed by the maṣdar.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِي أَطْعَمَهُمْ مِنْ جُوعٍ وَآمَنَهُمْ مِنْ خَوْفٍ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (مِنْ جُوعٍ) and (مِنْ خَوْفٍ): i.e. because of hunger.
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. He fed them while they were hungry. And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Quraysh
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾ ("for the accustoming of Quraysh"): there are three ways [of saying] it: ”لِإلافِ قُرَيْشٍ“, ﴿لإيلافِ قُرَيْشٍ﴾, and a third way, ”لِإلْفِ قُرَيْشٍ“. It has been read in the first two ways.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿إيلافِهِمْ رِحْلَةَ الشِّتاءِ والصَّيْفِ﴾ ("their accustoming to the journey of winter and summer"): what was permissible in ”لِإيلافِ“ is permissible in it, except that in this one it has been read ”إلْفِهِمْ“ and ”إيلافِهِمْ“, and ”إلافِهِمْ“ is permissible.
Regarding this lām, the grammarians gave three views. It was said: it is connected with what precedes it; the meaning is: "He made them like eaten-up straw for the accustoming of Quraysh", that is, Allah destroyed the people of the elephant so that Quraysh might remain, together with what they had become accustomed to of the journey of winter and summer. Some said: this is the lām of wonder (lām al-taʿajjub), so the meaning would be: "Wonder at the accustoming of Quraysh!" And the grammarians whose Arabic is approved said: this lām's sense is connected with what follows, ”فَلْيَعْبُدُوا“; the meaning is: "So let these worship the Lord of this House because of their accustoming to the journey of winter and summer."
The interpretation is that Quraysh used to travel in winter to Syria and in summer to Yemen and bring back provisions; they were safe on the two journeys while people [around them] were being snatched away. When anyone accosted them, they would say: "We are the people of Allah's Sanctuary", and they would not be molested. So Allah, Glorified is He, made known that what He did for these people is among the proofs of His oneness, because they were in a land without crops and yet they were safe in it. Allah, exalted be His praise, said: ﴿أوَلَمْ يَرَوْا أنّا جَعَلْنا حَرَمًا آمِنًا ويُتَخَطَّفُ النّاسُ مِن حَوْلِهِمْ أفَبِالباطِلِ يُؤْمِنُونَ وبِنِعْمَةِ اللَّهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 67] ("have they not seen that We made a secure Sanctuary while people are snatched away all around them? Do they then believe in falsehood and disbelieve in the favour of Allah?"), that is: they believe in the idols and disbelieve in Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, Who bestowed this favour upon them. So He commanded them to worship Him alone, because He had accustomed them to these two journeys.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿أطْعَمَهم مِن جُوعٍ﴾ ("Who fed them against hunger"): they had been afflicted by hardship until they ate carrion and carcasses. ﴿وَآمَنَهم مِن خَوْفٍ﴾ ("and made them safe from fear"): He made them safe from fearing in the Sanctuary and from fearing on their journey. One says ”ألِفْتُ المَكانَ، آلَفُهُ، إلْفًا“ ("I became accustomed to the place"), and ”آلَفْتُ المَكانَ“ in the sense of ”ألِفْتُ“, [with the forms] ”أوْلِفُهُ، إيلافًا“. [Translator's note: so in the source; the expected imperfect of «آلَفْتُ» is «أُولِفُهُ».]
